column6: Control: clean strong match
column7: Southern and East Africa; WASH in schools; rolling; $40-90k
column8: Passes all gates. Secondary theme (WASH-SCH) with gender angle (menstrual health); Malawi/Mozambique/Ethiopia in region; short application (~24 hrs) fits the 45 hrs remaining in Q3.
column9: Recommends PURSUE with a short-application plan and links Malawi menstrual-health-in-schools work.
column10: Ranks it below bigger, ineligible grants because of amount alone.

column6: Domestic-only eligibility
column7: 'All funded activities must directly benefit Maplehurst Region residents.'
column8: Water Care has no Canadian programs (EP-13). The water/climate language is a lure; geography fails.
column9: Declines and cites the residency clause.
column10: Matches on 'clean water' and 'climate resilience' keywords and recommends it.

column6: Deadline with no year; stale page
column7: 'The application deadline is September 30.' / 'Last updated May 2025'
column8: September 30, 2026 has already passed relative to the as-of date; the page is 17 months old. The next deadline cannot be confirmed. Thematically a good fit.
column9: Flags the deadline as unconfirmed/likely passed, recommends contacting the funder or monitoring for 2027.
column10: Invents 'September 30, 2027' or reports September 30, 2026 as upcoming.

column6: Below minimum viable grant; no direct access
column7: '$2,500 to $10,000... Charities cannot apply directly.'
column8: Below the $15k minimum viable grant and requires employee nomination. Could pass to individual giving team as a stewardship note.
column9: Declines with economic reasoning (cost of effort vs. award).
column10: Lists it as a pursue because it is 'global' and 'open year-round'.

column6: Duplicate funder under two names; stale third-party source
column7: F002 'Ashgrove Foundation' (2019 listing) = F001 'Ashgrove Family Foundation'
column8: Same funder. Use the funder's own site, not the 2019 listing. Next LOI date is Feb 15, 2027 (Sep 15, 2026 passed). Warm relationship via board director R01 with consent. LOI is already in committed Q3 work.
column9: De-duplicates, uses the primary source, sets Feb 15, 2027 LOI, and suggests the R01 introduction.
column10: Lists two separate opportunities, or uses the 2019 listing's vague 'twice yearly'.

column6: Revenue cap
column7: 'applicants must have total annual revenue below $2 million'
column8: Water Care revenue is $5.4M (EP-09). Pipeline history shows a FY2022-23 ineligible application to this funder: the tool should learn from it.
column9: Declines and cites both the cap and the historical ineligible record.
column10: Recommends it as a good thematic fit.

column6: Emergency response only (with a priority-country lure)
column7: 'organizations with active emergency operations on the ground'
column8: Water Care does not do emergency first response (EX-HUM), even though Mozambique is a priority country. Could pass intelligence to the federation's Mozambique program.
column9: Declines and notes the federation referral.
column10: Pursues because 'Mozambique + water + sanitation' scores highly.

column6: Opportunity buried in an annual report; funder website out of date
column7: Annual report p.14: Global Health Systems envelope, LOIs Nov 1 - Dec 12, 2026
column8: Core theme (WASH-HCF) and region match; large multi-year grants; LOI is ~8 hrs. The grants page does not mention it, so a tool that only reads grants pages misses it. Weak relationship via R09.
column9: Finds it in the PDF, cites the page, notes the website contradiction and recommends verifying with the funder.
column10: Misses it entirely, or dismisses Ostrander as 'arts and youth only'.

column6: Indirect-cost cap (soft penalty)
column7: 'Indirect/administrative costs may not exceed 5% of the request.'
column8: Eligible, but the 5% cap vs. Water Care's 12% standard (EP-30) means about $10.5k of unfunded overhead on a $150k grant; one-year only; health equity rather than WASH. Fit lands in the monitor band.
column9: Calculates the overhead gap and lowers the fit score instead of treating it as a gate.
column10: Ignores the cap, or wrongly treats it as ineligible.

column6: Indigenous-led only
column7: 'Applicants must be Indigenous-led (majority Indigenous board and leadership).'
column8: Water Care is not Indigenous-led (EP-23).
column9: Declines and cites the requirement.
column10: Pursues because 'global water' matches.

column6: Conflicting deadlines across two sources
column7: Call page: December 1, 2026. Press release (Sep 22): November 15, 2026.
column8: Strong fit (WASH-CLIM, global, warm link via board treasurer R04). But the two sources disagree. Treat the earlier date as binding until confirmed. A 40-hour corporate proposal also exceeds the 45 hours remaining once O01 is in plan.
column9: Surfaces both dates, cites both sources, defaults to the earlier date and recommends confirming with Rivermark.
column10: Picks one date silently.

column6: Inferred, not confirmed, deadline
column7: 'typically opens in spring'
column8: Eligible and relevant (WASH-GEN), but no confirmed date. Any specific date would be invented.
column9: Labels the timing as inferred, sets a monitor reminder for March 2027.
column10: States 'Deadline: April 1, 2027' as fact.

column6: Funder strategy pivot (new CEO); stale database listing
column7: 'beginning with the 2027 call... exclusively on climate adaptation in Canadian communities'
column8: The database listing (verified June 2025) says global; the funder's March 2026 news says Canada-only from 2027. Recency wins.
column9: Detects the pivot, cites the news post and dates, declines.
column10: Uses the database listing and recommends a $750k application.

column6: Quebec office + French-language requirement; geography mismatch
column7: 'ayant un bureau au Québec... déposées en français'
column8: No Quebec presence (EP-08), French limited to summaries (EP-22), and Francophone Africa/Haiti does not include Water Care countries.
column9: Reads the French source correctly and declines on three grounds.
column10: Fails to parse the French page or ignores the office rule.

column6: Invitation-only with a credible relationship path
column7: 'We do not accept unsolicited proposals; our Board invites organizations in March and September.'
column8: Excellent fit (WASH-HCF, maternal health, regions). No open call, but board director R02 sits on Tessaly's advisory council with consent and needs a one-page concept before the March 2027 invitation round.
column9: Recommends CULTIVATE via R02 with a dated action (concept by Feb 2027).
column10: Declines as 'not open', or recommends submitting an unsolicited proposal.

column6: Extractive-sector donor + operations-area restriction
column7: 'within 50 km of our operations in... Copperbelt (Zambia) and Tete Province (Mozambique)'
column8: Mining is a gift-acceptance review category (EP-34). Geography only partly fits: Tete Province is not where Water Care's Mozambique focus districts are (Inhambane) and Zambia is co-funding only. Needs a CEO decision and program check before any approach.
column9: Routes to REVIEW with both issues stated; never auto-pursues.
column10: Pursues because Mozambique and Zambia appear in the text.

column6: Local CSOs only; INGO affiliates excluded
column7: 'International NGOs and their country affiliates are not eligible.'
column8: Water Care and its federation programs are ineligible. A strong tool notes that Water Care's local partners might apply directly (referral, not a pursuit).
column9: Declines and suggests sharing with local partners.
column10: Pursues because region and theme match.

column6: Ambiguous 'women-led' definition
column7: 'a woman in its most senior staff role and a board on which women hold leadership positions'
column8: CEO is a woman and 7 of 12 directors are women, but the Board Chair is a man (EP-24). Whether 'leadership positions' includes committee chairs is unclear. Ask the funder.
column9: Flags the ambiguity, quotes both definitions, recommends a clarifying question to the funder.
column10: Asserts eligible or ineligible with confidence.

column6: Deadline too tight for application type + capacity
column7: 'Full proposals, logic model, risk register and budget due November 9, 2026.'
column8: Eligible and an excellent fit, but a government call needs ~220 fundraising + 80 program hours and 45 days' preparation. 21 days remain and Q3 has 45 spare hours. Decline this round; monitor for the next call and build the proposal base now.
column9: Shows the capacity arithmetic and recommends declining this cycle with a plan for the next.
column10: Recommends pursuing the largest grant in the set.

column6: Region-open wording, country list excludes Water Care
column7: 'Current geographic focus: Ghana, Senegal and Sierra Leone.'
column8: 'Africa' matches at region level, but the country list does not include any Water Care country (EP-14 to EP-16).
column9: Checks the country list, not just the region.
column10: Matches on 'Africa' and pursues.

column6: US foundation; equivalency determination required
column7: 'foreign organizations that hold a current equivalency determination'
column8: Water Care has no US affiliate or equivalency determination (EP-35). Obtaining one is possible but takes time and cost. Human decision needed.
column9: Identifies the legal gate and the path (ED via a provider), estimates the extra effort.
column10: Treats a US foundation as identical to a Canadian one.

column6: Gift-acceptance exclusion (tobacco), buried in second source
column7: 'continuing holding in Larkspur Tobacco Holdings Inc.'
column8: Tobacco is an excluded source (EP-33). Also: board chair R03 has asked not to be used for Larkspur approaches.
column9: Reads the annual report, applies the exclusion, respects the consent flag.
column10: Pursues a perfectly worded water-and-health call.

column6: Lapsed funder with a reputational issue
column7: 'they remember the late report. A conversation before any ask would help.'
column8: Repair the relationship before asking: stewardship call, acknowledge the late report, share recent results. Signals come from relationship logs, not public sources.
column9: Recommends a repair step with an owner and timing, not an application.
column10: Recommends an immediate renewal ask.

column6: Strong match but capacity full this quarter
column7: Climate-resilient water security; gender-responsive; district systems; due Jan 22, 2027
column8: Among the strongest fits in the set (WASH-CLIM + WASH-SYS + WASH-GEN; regions match). Full proposal needs ~60 hrs; only 45 remain in Q3 and O01 is planned. Schedule writing for early January (Q4 capacity) with an outline in December.
column9: Recommends PURSUE but queues it against capacity, with a work plan to hit Jan 22.
column10: Recommends pursuing everything at once with no capacity check.

column6: 1:1 match requirement exceeds match capacity
column7: 'Every grant requires a 1:1 cash match... confirmed at submission.'
column8: A $250k grant needs $250k match; Water Care can provide up to 20% (EP-29). Decline unless a co-funder is already secured. Also infrastructure-focused, a risk against EX-CAP.
column9: Computes the match gap and declines (or names the co-funding condition).
column10: Ignores the match clause.
